PROBLEM: Tool calls arrive as provider-shaped raw items with unstable identities; approvals, ledgers, and retries need one canonical identity per invocation.
MECHANISM: tool_invocation_identity() returns (invocation_type, provider call_id, SHA-256 fingerprint) where the fingerprint is over a normalized semantic payload: type, name, namespace, server_label, arguments/input/action/operation, environment, caller. Normalization sorts mapping keys, excludes None, parses JSON argument strings before hashing, and unwraps hosted-MCP approval request nesting. Covers function_call, mcp_approval_request, shell/local_shell/computer/apply_patch/custom tool calls. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/_tool_invocation.py
INVARIANT: Two invocations with identical normalized semantics produce identical fingerprints regardless of JSON key order or whitespace; distinct providers call IDs never collide in the same scope.
FAILURE_MODEL: Normalization falls back to str(value) for unrecognized types; if arguments cannot be parsed as JSON they are hashed as raw string. Identity computation never raises: unrecognized types return None.
SECURITY_MODEL: Fingerprint covers arguments/input/action but not secrets beyond what the caller passes; hosted MCP approval requests are unwrapped so the fingerprint describes the actual request. No cross-invocation auth is derived from the fingerprint alone.
SCALING_MODEL: O(size of semantic payload) SHA-256 per invocation; stateless pure function, no locks; thread-safe.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no durable per-attempt Run identity and no tool-execution path; the closest CRX concepts are idempotent deterministic IDs in MissionRuntime and fail-closed canonicalization at ingress.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX canonicalizes events at ingress; the SDK canonicalizes tool invocations at plan time and separates call identity (provider call_id) from semantic identity (fingerprint). CRX would need the semantic fingerprint for stable dedupe across retries, which provider call IDs alone do not give.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-moderate: port the normalization+fingerprint functions into CRX canonicalization as a ToolAttempt identity layer; wire into existing event canonicalization.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: gives CRX the missing per-attempt tool identity with retry-stable dedupe and scope-safe approval binding.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Implement the normalizer, then feed the same arguments with different JSON key order and whitespace and assert identical fingerprints; assert that dropping an argument field changes the fingerprint; assert unrecognized raw types return None instead of raising.

PROBLEM: An approval granted for one tool call must not silently authorize a different call: argument changes or namespace changes must invalidate the grant.
MECHANISM: tool_invocation_approval_scope() returns (invocation_type, scope_fingerprint) where the scope payload is type + invocation_role + the resolved function-tool lookup key (or tool name + MCP server_label for hosted MCP). Approvals bind to the scope fingerprint, not the call ID, so always_approve grants survive retries of the same scoped call but do not transfer to a different tool, namespace, or server. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/_tool_invocation.py
INVARIANT: Same scope fingerprint implies same authorization target; a different tool lookup key or server label always changes the fingerprint.
FAILURE_MODEL: If the lookup key cannot be resolved, approval scope returns None and the caller must fail closed (no scope, no cached approval).
SECURITY_MODEL: Scope deliberately excludes raw arguments for function tools (keyed by lookup key instead), trading per-argument granularity for a stable grant; argument-level binding lives in the semantic fingerprint, not the approval scope.
SCALING_MODEL: Same cost as the identity fingerprint; cached per run in the approval map.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX action-level authorization is absent (ingress only). This is the closest working model of action-scope authorization keys.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX authorizes at ingress; the SDK authorizes per tool invocation with a two-level key (scope for grants, semantic fingerprint for exactness). CRX adopting scope fingerprints would move authorization from ingress-only to per-action without conflating call identity with grant identity.
INTEGRATION_COST: Moderate: add an authorization-scope key to CRX worker tool calls, derived from the canonicalized tool reference rather than the attempt ID.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: closes part of the action-level authorization gap with a proven two-level key design.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Grant always_approve for tool A, then invoke tool A with a different MCP server_label and assert the cached approval does not apply; assert approval scope resolution returns None for a call missing its lookup key.

PROBLEM: A run must know which tool invocations were planned, which actually executed, and which completed, across pauses, resumes, and retries.
MECHANISM: _ToolInvocationRecord{invocation_type, approval_scope, fingerprint, executed, completed} is stored per provider call ID in RunContextWrapper._tool_invocations. _mark_tool_invocation_executed is called before execution (including on the rejection path, so rejections are recorded), _mark_tool_call_completed after. RunState._serialize_tool_invocations persists the ledger, described in source as the run-owned canonical tool invocation ledger, and from_json rebuilds it. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_context.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_state.py
INVARIANT: executed=True implies the invocation left the planning stage exactly once per recorded call ID; completed=True implies a receipt was recorded; the ledger survives serialization round-trips with identical records.
FAILURE_MODEL: Duplicate call IDs across nested agent-tool runs raise UserError rather than merging (distinct call IDs required). Restored ledgers mark unbound approvals explicitly.
SECURITY_MODEL: Ledger keys are provider call IDs; collisions across nested runs are rejected loudly instead of merged, preventing one run's approval from authorizing another run's call.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-call dict entry; serialization is O(n) over invocations; no global locks, run-local state.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX worker results reify as canonical events; CRX lacks a per-attempt run ledger. The ledger maps to a CRX Run-scoped projection of TOOL ATTEMPT / TOOL RECEIPT events.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX records worker results as events but has no attempt/completion lifecycle flags per tool call. The SDK's ledger gives the exact state machine (planned, executed, completed) CRX's proven gaps list is missing.
INTEGRATION_COST: Moderate: add executed/completed lifecycle to CRX tool-attempt events and a run-scoped projection; adopt the duplicate-call-ID loud-failure rule.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: directly addresses CRX's no-durable-per-attempt-Run-identity gap.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Serialize a RunState mid-run, restore it, and assert the invocation ledger round-trips with executed/completed flags intact; inject a duplicate call ID across a nested agent-tool run and assert UserError.

PROBLEM: A tool output must be joinable to the exact invocation that produced it, even when outputs arrive as provider-shaped items with different type names.
MECHANISM: tool_output_identity() maps output types (function_call_output, mcp_approval_response, shell_call_output, etc.) back to (invocation_type, call_id), handling the special case where mcp_approval_response joins on approval_request_id instead of call_id. The runner uses this to mark completions and to attribute receipts. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/_tool_invocation.py
INVARIANT: Every recognized output type maps to exactly one invocation type; the join key is always the provider's own ID field, never a derived value.
FAILURE_MODEL: Unrecognized output types return None; callers treat None as unjoinable rather than guessing.
SECURITY_MODEL: Join uses provider IDs only; no semantic inference, so a spoofed output cannot be attributed to an invocation whose call_id it does not carry.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX TOOL RECEIPT is absent; CRX worker results reify as events but are not joined to attempts by a typed rule.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX would need to add the output-to-attempt join as canonicalization logic. The SDK shows the join must handle provider-specific ID fields (approval_request_id) as first-class cases, not generic call_id reads.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: implement as a pure function in CRX canonicalization mapping receipt events to attempt IDs.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: makes TOOL RECEIPT provable as a join rather than a convention.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Feed an mcp_approval_response item and assert it joins on approval_request_id, not call_id; feed an unknown output type and assert None; assert no two output types map to the same invocation type ambiguously.

PROBLEM: An agent run needs a small, stable vocabulary of recorded units so tooling can reason about runs without parsing free text.
MECHANISM: Typed span data classes: task (one Runner.run), turn (one loop turn), agent, generation (one model call with input/output/model/sanitized config/usage), response (provider response_id), function (tool call with input/output/mcp_data), handoff (from_agent/to_agent), guardrail (name/triggered), mcp_tools (server/tool list), custom (name + data bag), plus voice spans. Emitted at fixed code points; task/turn spans gated by a config flag defaulting to true. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tracing/span_data.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tracing/create.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/models/_trace.py
INVARIANT: Every emitted span has a typed data payload, a parent link, and start/finish; span skeletons exist even when sensitive payloads are redacted.
FAILURE_MODEL: Spans are best-effort telemetry: export failures must not fail the run; disabled tracing yields NoOp spans that preserve API shape.
SECURITY_MODEL: Span payloads are the exfiltration surface: see the sensitive-data gating mechanism. Metadata dicts are user-controlled and must be treated as untrusted by exporters.
SCALING_MODEL: Spans are created per unit of work; batch export via BatchTraceProcessor amortizes backend calls.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has a canonical event journal with causation/correlation lineage but empty observability tables; the SDK's taxonomy is the closest worked example of a minimal serious span vocabulary.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX's journal is event-sourced and canonical; the SDK's trace is telemetry, exported by default to a vendor backend. The harvestable part is the ten-type vocabulary and the fixed emission points, not the storage.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: map the ten span types onto CRX event types; keep CRX's journal as the store, adopt only the vocabulary and emission points.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: gives CRX the missing observability vocabulary without a second storage system.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run an agent with tracing enabled and assert one task span, N turn spans, one generation span per model call, one function span per tool call with parent linkage intact; disable tracing and assert the run still completes with NoOp spans.

PROBLEM: Safety checks must halt the run fail-closed and still leave an auditable record of what tripped.
MECHANISM: Input/output guardrails run per turn; tool input/output guardrails run per tool call. Each emits a guardrail span with name and triggered bool. Results are appended to a results sink as each guardrail completes, including the tripping result, before the tripwire exception (Input/Output/ToolInput/ToolOutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered) propagates. Both streamed and non-streamed paths use the same sink discipline. A tripwire also attaches a SpanError to the current/parent span. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/guardrails.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tracing/span_data.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/exceptions.py
INVARIANT: A tripped guardrail always leaves both a span record (triggered=true) and a results-sink entry; no exit path can omit a result that already finished.
FAILURE_MODEL: Guardrail functions run concurrently; on a trip, siblings are cancelled and awaited so none leak past the function return. Guardrail exceptions propagate as typed tripwire exceptions, never as silent skips.
SECURITY_MODEL: Guardrails see full input/output including sensitive data; their results may carry excerpts. Treat guardrail outputs as sensitive payloads in any export.
SCALING_MODEL: Guardrails run concurrently per stage (asyncio tasks), so check latency is max, not sum, of guardrail latencies.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has fail-closed canonicalization at ingress and typed failure semantics; guardrail tripwires are the SDK's closest analog for policy verification with audit.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX fails closed at ingress; the SDK fails closed at four checkpoints (input, output, tool-input, tool-output) and records the trip in the sink even as it raises. CRX's VERIFICATION slot can adopt the record-before-raise discipline directly.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-moderate: adopt the record-before-raise sink discipline for CRX verification checkpoints; map tripwire types onto CRX typed failures.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: turns verification from a gate into auditable evidence.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Trip an output guardrail and assert the result appears in both the span data (triggered=true) and the results sink despite the exception; assert sibling guardrails are cancelled, not leaked.

PROBLEM: Every function-tool-backed run item must record where the tool came from: local function, MCP server, or a nested agent.
MECHANISM: ToolOrigin{type: function|mcp|agent_as_tool, mcp_server_name, agent_name, agent_tool_name} is a frozen serializable dataclass with to_json_dict/from_json_dict. It is stamped onto ToolCallItem/ToolCallOutputItem at creation when _emit_tool_origin is true, and it round-trips through RunState serialization. MCP tools additionally carry _mcp_tool_binding (original server name, raw tool name, server position) for resume. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tool.py
INVARIANT: Every function-tool item emitted by the runtime carries an origin that deserializes to a valid ToolOriginType; unknown types fail closed to None, never to a guessed type.
FAILURE_MODEL: from_json_dict returns None on malformed input instead of raising; callers must handle absent origin.
SECURITY_MODEL: Origin metadata distinguishes trust domains (local code vs remote MCP server vs nested agent); consumers must not treat a function-origin tool and an MCP-origin tool as equivalent privilege.
SCALING_MODEL: Zero per-call cost beyond a small dataclass; serialized only when items serialize.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no MCP/tool-execution path and no tool-origin concept; worker results reify as canonical events without origin typing.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX events lack origin typing entirely. ToolOrigin gives CRX the minimal trust-domain label (three values) that makes an MCP path auditable later.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: add a three-valued origin field to CRX tool-attempt events with strict deserialization.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prerequisite provenance for any future CRX MCP integration; cheap to add now.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Serialize a ToolCallItem from an MCP tool, deserialize the origin, and assert type=mcp with the server name intact; feed a forged origin type string and assert from_json_dict returns None.

PROBLEM: A run that needs human approval must pause durably, survive serialization, and resume exactly where it stopped without re-executing the unapproved call.
MECHANISM: Unapproved invocations become ToolApprovalItem interruptions; the step becomes NextStepInterruption. RunState.to_json serializes interruptions with agent identity maps and MCP tool bindings; from_json rebuilds them. state.approve(item, always_approve) / state.reject(item, always_reject, rejection_message) record decisions into _ApprovalRecord (approved/rejected lists, rejection messages, sticky scope). Re-running with the restored state continues past the interruption; the unapproved call is never executed. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/items.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_state.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_context.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/run_steps.py
INVARIANT: An interrupted run resumes with the identical pending approval set after a serialize/deserialize round-trip; approve() followed by rerun executes the approved call exactly once.
FAILURE_MODEL: ToolApprovalItem equality is object identity, so resume paths must re-resolve items through _find_current_approval_item by canonical identity, not by object reference. Nested agent-tool approvals are routed to the nested state.
SECURITY_MODEL: Approvals are a privilege boundary: always_approve grants are keyed by approval scope fingerprint, and nested-run call-ID collisions are rejected rather than merged, so one run cannot spend another run's approval.
SCALING_MODEL: Interruptions are a list on the run state; approval records are per-key dicts; all O(1) per decision.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no human-approval path in the execution loop; the SDK shows approvals as durable run-state, not ephemeral UI.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX authorizes only at ingress. The SDK shows the missing shape: approval as a first-class run-state transition (interruption), with decisions recorded durably and scoped by fingerprint. This is the AUTHORIZATION slot's executable form.
INTEGRATION_COST: Moderate-high: requires a pausable execution state machine in CRX WorkerRuntime, which does not currently exist.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: closes the human-approval gap with a design that survives process restarts.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Interrupt a run on an unapproved tool, serialize, deserialize, approve, resume, and assert the tool executed exactly once and the pending set is empty; attempt to approve with a stale object reference and assert identity-based re-resolution.

PROBLEM: MCP tool discovery is a trust-relevant event: the tool set an agent sees can change between runs as servers update.
MECHANISM: Every list_tools call against an MCP server is wrapped in an mcp_tools span recording the server name and the resulting tool name list (MCPListToolsSpanData). Discovery is therefore in the trace even when no tool is ever called. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/mcp/util.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tracing/span_data.py
INVARIANT: A list_tools call always produces a span with the server identity; an empty result is recorded as an empty list, not as a missing span.
FAILURE_MODEL: Span emission must not fail the discovery call; discovery errors are surfaced by the caller, not the span.
SECURITY_MODEL: The tool list is a capability snapshot; consumers must treat it as time-bound, since server tool sets can change.
SCALING_MODEL: One span per discovery call; discovery results should be cached by the MCP manager to avoid per-turn cost.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no MCP path at all; this is the smallest auditable unit of MCP provenance.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX has nothing to compare; this is a green-field addition. The insight is that discovery itself is a provenance event, not just invocations.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: emit a discovery event whenever CRX (future) MCP tooling lists server tools.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Low-medium: small now, but it is the seed of MCP auditability.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Point the manager at a test MCP server, call list_tools, and assert one mcp_tools span exists with the server name and the exact tool list, including the empty-list case.

PROBLEM: Multi-agent delegation needs a representation the model can invoke and the runtime can audit as a transfer of control, not just another function call.
MECHANISM: A handoff is a Handoff dataclass rendered to the model as a tool (default name transfer_to_<agent>). When invoked, the runner resolves the target agent, emits a handoff span (from_agent set at start, to_agent set after resolution), creates a HandoffOutputItem{source_agent, target_agent}, fires on_handoff hooks, and applies an optional input_filter to the next agent's model input. Only the first handoff per turn is honored; extras are ignored with a recorded SpanError. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/handoffs/__init__.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/turn_resolution.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/items.py
INVARIANT: A completed handoff always leaves a handoff span with both endpoints and a HandoffOutputItem naming source and target; control transfers to exactly one agent per turn.
FAILURE_MODEL: Multiple handoffs in one turn: first wins, rest are ignored and recorded. Target agent resolution failures propagate as run errors.
SECURITY_MODEL: input_filter is NOT a redaction mechanism: it filters model input only, while nested handoff history is built from input_history, pre_handoff_items, and new_items. Treating it as redaction leaks history across trust boundaries (documented in source).
SCALING_MODEL: One span plus one output item per handoff; hooks run concurrently via gather.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX parent agents spawn disposable subagents with no transcript inheritance and automatic result delivery; the SDK handoff is the closest formal delegation primitive.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX subagent spawning is heavier and transcript-isolated; the SDK handoff keeps one trace and forwards filtered history to the next agent. CRX should not adopt the mechanism, but the audit shape (span with both endpoints + output item naming source/target + fail-closed multi-delegation) is the pattern for recording delegation.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: adopt the delegation-record shape (from/to span + source/target output item) for CRX subagent spawn events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: gives CRX delegation edges the provenance its parent/subagent model currently lacks.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Invoke two handoffs in one turn and assert only the first transfers control while the span carries a Multiple handoffs requested error; assert the HandoffOutputItem names both source and target agents.

PROBLEM: An agent invoked as a tool needs full agent capabilities (its own loop, tools, guardrails) without surrendering the outer run's control flow or trace.
MECHANISM: Agent.as_tool() wraps the agent as a FunctionTool flagged _is_agent_tool with ToolOriginType.AGENT_AS_TOOL. Invocation runs a nested Runner run; nested results are registered in module-level maps keyed by tool-call object identity plus a stable signature (ScopedToolCallSignature) so call-ID collisions across nested runs cannot merge results. The nested run exposes agent_tool_invocation metadata; custom_output_extractor shapes what returns to the outer model. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/agent.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/agent_tool_state.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tool.py
INVARIANT: A nested agent-tool run never merges its results or approvals with the outer run or a sibling nested run, even under provider call-ID reuse.
FAILURE_MODEL: Nested runs add recursion risk; the SDK relies on max_turns and the signature-scoped registry rather than a depth counter. on_stream backpressure beyond on_stream_max_pending_events cancels the nested run and fails the tool through failure_error_function.
SECURITY_MODEL: The nested agent's tools execute with the outer run's context wrapper shared selectively (_share_tool_state_with); approval state is scoped so nested approvals do not leak outward.
SCALING_MODEL: Module-level registries keyed by object identity plus signature; entries must be cleaned up to avoid leaks across many nested calls.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX spawns disposable subagents per delegation; the SDK nests a full run inside a tool call with collision-safe result routing.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX's subagent model is transcript-isolated and parent-delivered; the SDK's is trace-shared and tool-scoped. Do not merge the models; watch the collision-safe registry design as the failure case CRX will hit if it ever nests runs inside tool calls.
INTEGRATION_COST: None now; revisit only if CRX adds nested execution.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Low direct value now; high option value if CRX ever needs agents inside tool calls.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run two nested agent-tools whose provider reuses a call ID and assert their results and approvals stay separate; exceed on_stream_max_pending_events and assert the nested run is cancelled and the tool fails through failure_error_function.

PROBLEM: Long-running agent work must be pausable to durable storage and resumable without losing approvals, invocation records, usage, or trace continuity.
MECHANISM: RunState.to_json() serializes: original input, generated/session items, model responses, turn counters, usage, context payload (with a serializer hook and strict mode), approvals (approved/rejected lists, rejection messages, sticky scope), the canonical tool invocation ledger, hosted MCP approvals, interruptions with agent identity maps and MCP bindings, and TraceState (trace_id, workflow name, group_id, metadata, plus a SHA-256 fingerprint of the tracing API key, never the key). from_json()/from_string() rebuild all of it; resume reattaches the same trace via ReattachedTrace without re-emitting trace start. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_state.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/tracing/traces.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_context.py
INVARIANT: A serialize/deserialize round-trip preserves the pending interruption set, approval records, invocation ledger flags, and trace identity exactly.
FAILURE_MODEL: Context payloads may be non-serializable; strict mode raises instead of silently dropping. Secrets in context are the caller's problem: docs warn against putting secrets in context intended for persistence (docs/context.md:53).
SECURITY_MODEL: Trace API keys persist as fingerprints only; raw keys are opt-in via include_tracing_api_key. Approval records persist grant history, which is itself sensitive.
SCALING_MODEL: Snapshot size is O(items + invocations + approvals); intended for database/queue storage between pauses, not per-turn writes.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX persists run ledgers as JSONL and uses git worktrees ad hoc; it lacks a unified durable run snapshot.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX's journal is append-only and canonical; the SDK's snapshot is a mutable resume blob. The harvestable idea is the snapshot's field list (what a serious runtime persists: interruptions, approvals, invocation ledger, trace continuity) as a checklist for CRX's durable run state, not the blob format.
INTEGRATION_COST: Moderate: define CRX's durable run-snapshot field list from this checklist; store as events/projections, not a blob.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-high: gives CRX the durable pause/resume state it needs for human-in-the-loop without inventing the field list from scratch.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Round-trip a mid-run state through to_json/from_json and assert interruptions, approvals, ledger flags, usage, and trace_id are identical; assert the tracing API key is absent unless explicitly included.

PROBLEM: Retries and resume can resend work to the provider, repeating real-world side effects; the runtime must make that danger explicit rather than hiding it.
MECHANISM: ModelRetrySettings with RetryDecision: the runner retries safe transport errors by policy, but docs state the bound plainly: if a retry policy returns RetryDecision(approve_unsafe_replay=True) after a request may have reached the provider, the runner can resend staged input and provider-side work can repeat. This SDK occurrence guarantee is not a provider-delivery guarantee. Durable orchestration across restarts is delegated to Dapr, Temporal, and Restate integrations (docs/running_agents.md:568-582); the SDK itself offers no exactly-once effect semantics. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/retry.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/docs/results.md; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/docs/running_agents.md
INVARIANT: The SDK never claims exactly-once effects; any replay path that can resend provider work requires an explicit unsafe-replay approval.
FAILURE_MODEL: A retry after an ambiguous provider response may double-execute; the failure model is documented, not prevented.
SECURITY_MODEL: approve_unsafe_replay is an explicit human/system opt-in to a known-unsafe action; the naming forces the caller to acknowledge the risk.
SCALING_MODEL: Retry policies are evaluated per model call; no global retry state.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has typed failure semantics (never silently convert failure to empty success) and delegates durability to a lane; the SDK's explicit unsafe-replay bound matches CRX's honesty principle.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX and the SDK agree: no exactly-once effects at this layer. The delta is documentation discipline: the SDK names the unsafe decision in the type system (RetryDecision.approve_unsafe_replay) instead of a boolean flag.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: name CRX's own replay hazards with the same explicitness in its retry/failure types.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prevents the most dangerous silent behavior (hidden double-execution) by making it a named, explicit decision.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Configure a retry policy returning approve_unsafe_replay=True after an ambiguous send and assert provider-side work repeats; assert the default policy does not retry ambiguous sends.

PROBLEM: Cost attribution needs per-request granularity, not just run totals, because cached tokens, reasoning tokens, and retried requests change the bill.
MECHANISM: Usage accumulates requests, input/output/total tokens plus input/output token details (cached, cache_write, reasoning). Every add() also appends a RequestUsage entry, giving a per-request list for cost calculation. Generation spans carry usage snapshots via model_usage_to_span_usage, and turn/task spans carry usage too. serialize_usage/deserialize_usage round-trip through RunState. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/usage.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/models/_trace.py
INVARIANT: Per-request entries sum to the run totals; a retried request appears as its own entry rather than being folded invisibly.
FAILURE_MODEL: Providers that report no usage still record requests=1 so streamed and non-streamed tracing stay aligned.
SECURITY_MODEL: Usage data is non-sensitive metadata but can reveal workload patterns; treat per-request lists as operational telemetry.
SCALING_MODEL: O(1) per request append; list grows with request count, bounded by max_turns in practice.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no usage accounting in its event model; this is a green-field pattern.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX's journal records what happened; the SDK shows cost belongs beside the model-call record, per request, with retry visibility. No conflict, pure addition.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: add per-request usage entries to CRX model-call events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Low-medium: enables cost attribution CRX currently cannot do.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Make three model calls with one retry and assert four RequestUsage entries whose token sums equal the run totals.

PROBLEM: An unbounded agent loop must terminate deterministically and leave evidence of why it stopped.
MECHANISM: max_turns is checked per turn; exceeding it attaches a SpanError (Max turns exceeded, with the limit) to the current agent span and raises MaxTurnsExceeded. Configured RunErrorHandlers can instead synthesize a final output, which is validated against the agent's output schema before being committed. The streamed path records whether the handler ran. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/run_loop.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/exceptions.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_error_handlers.py
INVARIANT: A run that exceeds max_turns always terminates and always leaves either the exception or a validated synthesized output plus the span error; it never loops silently.
FAILURE_MODEL: Handler exceptions propagate; a handler that returns invalid output fails validation rather than committing bad output.
SECURITY_MODEL: A synthesized final output is model-visible content produced by policy, not the agent; consumers must be able to distinguish it (it is committed as a message output item like any final output, so downstream readers should check the span error).
CRX_ANALOG: CRX already practices bounded automation with typed failure semantics; this corroborates rather than invents.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: No semantic conflict. The SDK's addition is attaching the bound violation to the trace (SpanError on the agent span) so the stop is visible in telemetry, not just in the exception.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: attach bound-violation evidence to CRX's existing typed failures.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Low: small telemetry improvement on a practice CRX already follows.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Set max_turns=1 on a two-turn task and assert MaxTurnsExceeded plus a SpanError on the agent span carrying the limit; configure a handler and assert its output passes schema validation before commit.

PROBLEM: Traces must be useful for debugging without becoming a secret-exfiltration channel when exported to third-party backends.
MECHANISM: trace_include_sensitive_data (default from OPENAI_AGENTS_TRACE_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_DATA, default true) gates all sensitive payloads: tool call arguments and outputs in function spans, generation inputs/outputs, error message contents (via get_trace_tool_error). Span skeletons (names, types, parent links, triggered flags) are always recorded. Model config URLs are sanitized (auth material and query params stripped) before entering spans. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_config.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py; https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/models/_trace.py
INVARIANT: Disabling the flag removes all sensitive payloads while preserving span structure; no code path can leak arguments into a span when the flag is false.
FAILURE_MODEL: The default is true, so a deployment that never sets the flag exports sensitive data to the configured trace backend by default. Failing closed would be the safer default; the SDK chose debuggability.
SECURITY_MODEL: This is the primary exfiltration control for the trace pipeline; exporters must additionally treat user metadata dicts as untrusted.
SCALING_MODEL: One boolean check per span write; sanitization is O(URL length).
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has fail-closed canonicalization at ingress; the SDK's trace gating is a parallel fail-open-by-default control CRX should invert.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX should adopt the skeleton-always/payload-gated split but default the gate to closed. The SDK's mistake to avoid copying is the default-true.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: split CRX observability payloads into skeleton vs sensitive with a default-closed gate.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prevents the trace pipeline from becoming a secret leak; the default matters more than the mechanism.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Set trace_include_sensitive_data=false, run a tool-calling agent, and assert function spans exist with names but null input/output; assert a base URL with credentials appears sanitized in generation span config.
